worked_solution:
Let $f(t)=5t$ represent the rate at which water enters the tank, and let $V(T)$ be the total volume of water in the tank after $T$ minutes.

Using our formula for the accumulation of change, we have

$$
V(T)=V(0)+{\int }_{0}^{T}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Substituting the known information and carrying out the necessary integration gives

$$
\begin{aligned}V(T) & =V(0)+{\int }_{0}^{T}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =40+{\int }_{0}^{T}5t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={40+(\frac{5{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{T} \\  & =40+\frac{5{T}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's rewrite our final answer in terms of the original variable  $t.$ We have

$$
V(t)=40+\frac{5{t}^{2}}{2}.
$$
